scientific_rubric.description: Identity and scope: Keep the full TTA derivative graphs and define charge/state and molecular reference consistently. Distinguish orbital eigenvalues, ionization energetics, work functions and actual transferred charge. For an interface claim, document the chosen nanotube/coverage/geometry and why its model scope is applicable. Respect differing compositions and loadings.

Quantitative scientific results: Quantify relevant electronic differences with raw molecular or interface evidence, explicit reference conventions and applicability to the source system. Assess the claim being tested rather than merely reprinting three frontier levels.

Evidence that distinguishes the claimed explanation: Investigate whether the molecular/interface evidence supports a plausible explanation of differences and confront the relevant confounding factors. The agent chooses the model and tests; no adsorption motif or transport solver is mandatory.

Uncertainty and limits: Assess numerical/model dependence and whether differences are resolvable. Explicitly delimit missing nanotube ensemble/morphology/loading information and avoid treating it as a failure of the agent to recover a nonexistent unique structure.

Bounded answer to the question: Give a bounded account of electronic differences relevant to SWCNT interaction and the supported extent of the composite explanation. Unsupported transfer or thermoelectric claims must be withheld even when the molecular calculations are sound.

scoring_notes: AR and PR share result validity; actual open_research runtime supplies mode-specific process rubrics.
Source author outcomes are conditional reference evidence, not mandatory winners. No inherited numerical tolerance.
No penalty simply for a different justified model, hypothesis count, metric or valid analysis route. Scientific adequacy is claim-dependent.
Completion requires a substantiated answer to the stated question. Honest partial credit is distinct from passing all scientific criteria.
